sections.heading: Identity and current status

- Project ID: `hermes-agent`
- Canonical name: Hermes Agent (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-identity`)
- Current status: active public release; latest checked release Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (v2026.8.16), dated August 16, 2026 (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-status`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-version`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-maintenance`)

- Availability: native desktop on macOS, Windows, and Linux; Termux on Android is Tier 2 (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-availability`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: the self-improving AI agent built by Nous Research — an autonomous agent with a built-in learning loop that creates skills from experience and persists knowledge across sessions (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-unique-value`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-identity`)
- What it is not: not a coding copilot tethered to an IDE or a chatbot wrapper around a single API (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-not-for-copilot`). Hermes 4 is a Nous chat/reasoning model family, not this agent product, and is not recommended as the in-agent runtime model (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-not-hermes-4`). Editorial only, no first-party quote: this catalogue row is not HP-Linux Rune (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-not-hp-linux-rune`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a catalogue taxonomy inference from `AIAgent` in `run_agent.py` owning the loop; pages do not use `runtime` as a product-type label (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: Hermes / Nous Research. The core orchestration engine is `run_agent.py`'s `AIAgent` class (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-agent-loop-owner`)
- Architecture: one `AIAgent` class serves CLI, gateway, ACP, batch, and API server; platform differences live in the entry point (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-architecture`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface ledger rows were not written this pass. First-party surfaces in prose:
  - Interactive CLI / TUI via `hermes` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-surface-cli`)
  - Native desktop app on macOS, Windows, and Linux; same core, not a separate product (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-surface-desktop`)
  - Messaging gateway: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI from one process; docs index also lists 20+ platforms (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-surface-gateway`)
  - OpenAI-compatible API and ACP editor integration (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-api`)
  - Termux on Android (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-mobile-access`)
- Execution location: the machine that runs Hermes — local device, a cloud VM you operate, or another `hermes serve` host. It is not tied to the laptop (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-execution-location`)
- Platform compatibility: macOS, Windows, Linux desktop; Termux Android Tier 2 (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-availability`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: any model — Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, your own endpoint, and others; switch with `hermes model` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-model-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: bring-your-own keys / own endpoint, or optional Nous Portal OAuth. Portal is recommended but not required (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-auth-strategy`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-byok`)
- Provider support: cloud APIs and self-hosted endpoints including Ollama and vLLM; any OpenAI-compatible API (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-local-models`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-model-strategy`)
- BYOK: `supported` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-byok`)
- Local models: `supported` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-local-models`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: at least 64,000 tokens of context for agent use with tools (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-context-behavior`)
- Memory: bounded, curated memory that persists across sessions in `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md`; optional external providers are documented (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-memory`)
- Compaction: unknown as a named product compaction feature. The loop docs mention compression as an `AIAgent` responsibility; that is not promoted to a standalone compaction claim
- Session behavior: gateway adapters route through a per-chat session store to `AIAgent` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-architecture`). Memory persists across sessions (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-memory`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: a broad built-in registry covering web search, browser automation, terminal execution, file editing, memory, delegation, scheduled tasks, Home Assistant, and more. First-party pages disagree on the count (README 40+, docs index 60+, architecture 70+). Recorded, not averaged (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: unknown as a separate extension product. Plugin hooks and the Tool Gateway are documented (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-hooks`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-tool-gateway`)
- MCP: client for local stdio and remote HTTP servers, a curated catalog, and `hermes mcp serve` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: on-demand documents compatible with agentskills.io; the agent can create, update, and delete its own skills via `skill_manage` (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-skills`)
- Hooks: four systems — Gateway, Plugin, Shell, and Outbound webhooks (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: OpenAI-compatible API; ACP stdio/JSON-RPC for VS Code, Zed, and JetBrains; embed `AIAgent` in Python scripts (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-api`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: `AIAgent` owns prompt assembly, tool dispatch, retries, fallback, compression, and persistence (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-agent-loop-owner`). Delegation and scheduled tasks appear in the tool registry (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-tools`). A separate orchestration-product claim was not written
- Parallelism: unknown

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: seven terminal backends — local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, and Vercel Sandbox. Local runs on the host (no isolation). Docker applies container hardening. Homepage copy lists five backends; README lists seven. Recorded, not averaged. Do not flatten to a single Yes/No (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-isolation`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-tag-sandbox`)
- Permissions: dangerous-command check; default `smart` approval; YOLO bypasses prompts for the session; a blocklist remains the floor. Gateway denies users not on an allowlist or paired via DM (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-permissions`)
- Security: eight-layer model including user authorization, dangerous-command approval, and container isolation. Docker: `--cap-drop ALL`, `--security-opt no-new-privileges`, `--pids-limit 256`. Write guards are defense-in-depth, not a hard boundary (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-security`)
- Data path: unknown as an exact on-disk layout. Memory files `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` persist across sessions (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-memory`)

Tool Gateway is included with every paid Portal subscription, pay-as-you-use; Free-tier Portal accounts can use inference but not managed tools (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-tool-gateway`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: vendor positions it as the self-improving autonomous agent with a built-in learning loop (skills from experience, persist knowledge, search past conversations). The superlative "only" is their marketing claim, not a Compare fact (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-unique-value`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: the local terminal backend runs on the host and is not a sandbox against a deliberately adversarial process; write guards are not a hard boundary; Termux has no Docker isolation (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-drawback-local-host`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-isolation`, `claim-hermes-agent-sf-mobile-access`)
- Best fit: unknown as a first-party audience sentence. Docs position it as a terminal-native autonomous coding and task agent (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-execution-location`)
- Not-for: not an IDE copilot or single-API chatbot wrapper (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-not-for-copilot`); Hermes 4 models are not recommended as the agent runtime model (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-not-hermes-4`); editorial not-for HP-Linux Rune (`claim-hermes-agent-sf-not-hp-linux-rune`)
